examples.en: My favorite subject is math.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 교과목이 두 개 늘었어요.
examples.en: Two subjects were added this semester.
Each subject has a different teacher.
Which subject is the hardest?
Please check the subject timetable.
In the new subject we learn coding.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '과목'이라고 하는 일이 더 많고, '교과목'은 학교 안내문이나 시간표처럼 딱딱한 문서에서 자주 보여요. 국어, 수학, 영어 같은 하나하나를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: What is the hardest subject?
phrases.nuance_ko: '교과목'과 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 교과목, and more common in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 수학은 모든 학생이 배워야 하는 필수 교과목이에요.
phrases.en: Math is a required subject that all students must take.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 들어야 하는 과목을 말할 때 학교 안내문에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in school notices for subjects everyone must take.

phrases.en: The teacher is different for each subject.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과목마다 나눠서 말할 때 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something applies to each subject separately.

explain_en: In daily speech people more often just say '과목', while '교과목' shows up in formal documents such as school notices and timetables. It refers to each individual subject like 국어, 수학 or 영어.

examples.en: My grandfather farms dry fields.
In this area there is more field farming than rice-paddy farming.
Field farming is hard when there is little rain.
Chili peppers and beans are mostly grown in dry fields.
I went to buy plastic sheeting for farming the field.
We were short of hands for the field work, so the neighbors helped.

explain: 물을 대는 논에서 벼를 키우는 '논농사'와 짝이 되는 말이에요. 밭에서는 채소, 콩, 고추 같은 것을 키워요. '농사를 짓다'는 ㅅ 불규칙이라 '밭농사를 지어요'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: My parents farm fields in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농사를 짓다'의 기본 짝말로, 밭에서 하는 농사를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard pairing with '농사를 짓다', meaning farming in dry fields.

phrases.example: 이 마을은 논농사와 밭농사를 모두 해요.
phrases.en: This village does both rice-paddy and field farming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 말이 짝이 되어 함께 나오는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two words are a pair and often appear together.

phrases.en: Field farming is very hard in the summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밭에서 하는 일의 어려움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how hard the work in the field is.

explain_en: It pairs with '논농사', growing rice in flooded paddies. In 밭, people grow things like vegetables, beans and chili peppers. '농사를 짓다' is a ㅅ-irregular verb, so you say '밭농사를 지어요'.

en: to be sorted; to be classified

examples.en: Books are sorted by subject.
These clothes were classified as winter clothes.
Please tell me the criteria for sorting.
There are many unsorted documents.
If trash is sorted by type, recycling is easy.
I put the sorted photos in a folder.

explain: 나뉘어서 어느 칸에 들어갈 때 써요. 조사 '으로/로'와 같이 '~로 분류되다'라고 말해요. 나누는 사람이 주어이면 '분류하다'예요.

phrases.en: The staff sorts the letters by region.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나누는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when the subject is the person doing the sorting.

phrases.en: The documents are sorted by number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 나뉘어 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where things are already sorted.

phrases.en: Trash is sorted by type.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준을 함께 말할 때 '~별로'를 자주 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The suffix ~별로 is often added to state the basis of sorting.

explain_en: Use it when something is divided and placed into a category. It goes with '으로/로', as in '~로 분류되다'. If a person does the sorting, use '분류하다'.

examples.ko: 강사님이 수강생들에게 컴퓨터 사용법을 차근차근 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The instructor explained step by step how to use the computer to the students.

examples.ko: 이번 요리 수업은 수강생이 열 명밖에 안 돼요.
examples.en: This cooking class has only ten students.
I signed up as a student in the English conversation class.

examples.ko: 수강생 여러분, 내일은 수업이 한 시간 일찍 시작해요.
examples.en: Everyone in the class, tomorrow's lesson starts an hour early.

examples.ko: 수강생이 많아서 강의실을 더 큰 곳으로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: There were so many students that we moved to a bigger classroom.

examples.ko: 학원에서 수강생들의 후기를 보고 반을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I read reviews from the students at the academy and picked a class.

explain: 학교에서는 보통 '학생'이라고 하고, 학원, 특강, 문화센터처럼 강좌를 듣는 곳에서 '수강생'을 많이 써요. 짝말은 '강사'예요.

phrases.en: We are recruiting students for the new class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학원이나 강좌에서 사람을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a class or academy is looking for students.

phrases.en: The number of students is gradually growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강좌의 인기가 높아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a course is becoming more popular.

phrases.example: 수강생 여러분은 다음 주까지 숙제를 내 주세요.
phrases.en: Students, please hand in your homework by next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강사가 여러 사람에게 말을 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by an instructor to address the whole class.

explain_en: At school people usually say '학생', while '수강생' is common at academies, special lectures and culture centers where you take a course. The counterpart is '강사' (instructor).

examples.en: In the old days, most things were made by handicraft industry.
This village is a place famous for its handicraft industry.
After the Industrial Revolution, handicraft manufacturing declined.

examples.ko: 수공업 제품은 값이 비싸지만 품질이 좋아요.
examples.en: Handmade products are expensive but of good quality.
I studied the difference between handicraft work and factory production.

examples.ko: 전통 수공업을 이어 가는 젊은 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of young people carrying on traditional handicrafts is growing.

explain: 손으로 직접 만드는 작은 규모의 생산이라서 기계로 대량 생산하는 '기계 공업'과 자주 비교돼요. '공예'는 아름다운 물건을 만드는 기술에 가깝고, '수공업'은 만드는 일이나 산업을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: This shop sells only handmade products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 만든 물건이라는 점을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say an item was made by hand.

phrases.en: Handicraft industry has developed in this region since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역이나 시대를 설명할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when describing a region or era.

phrases.en: My grandmother earned money through cottage industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 가족이 하는 작은 규모의 손일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to small-scale handwork done at home by a family.

explain_en: It is small-scale production made directly by hand, so it is often compared with machine-based mass production. '공예' is closer to the craft of making beautiful objects, while '수공업' is used for the work or industry of making things.

examples.ko: 자막에 오역이 있어서 이해가 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The subtitles had a mistranslation, so I couldn't follow.
The translator admitted the mistranslation and fixed the book.
A single mistranslation caused a big misunderstanding.
There are mistranslations in AI translation too.

examples.ko: 이 문장은 오역 때문에 뜻이 완전히 달라졌어요.
examples.en: Because of a mistranslation, this sentence's meaning changed completely.

examples.ko: 영화 팬들이 자막 오역을 찾아서 올렸어요.
examples.en: Movie fans found subtitle mistranslations and posted them.

explain: '오해', '오답', '오타'처럼 '오-'가 붙은 말은 잘못됐다는 느낌을 더해요. 번역할 때 생기는 실수는 오역, 말을 잘못 알아듣는 건 '오해'로 구별해요. '번역 실수'보다 짧고 글에 어울려요.

phrases.en: The translator mistranslated this sentence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 번역을 잘못했다는 동작을 말할 때 동사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, for the act of translating something wrongly.

phrases.example: 출판사가 책의 오역을 고쳐서 다시 냈어요.
phrases.en: The publisher fixed the mistranslations and reissued the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀린 번역을 바로잡을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when correcting a wrong translation.

phrases.example: 작은 번역 실수가 큰 오해를 만들었어요.
phrases.en: A small translation error caused a big misunderstanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오역보다 말이 길고 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Longer than 오역 but easier to use in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Words that start with '오-', like '오해', '오답' and '오타', add the sense of something being wrong. A mistake made in translating is 오역, while hearing something wrongly is '오해'. It is shorter than '번역 실수' and suits writing.

examples.en: The password has six digits.
Please check the number of digits in the phone number again.
When I calculate, I line up the digits.
Numbers with many digits are hard to read.
The number goes through as long as the digit count is right.

examples.ko: 일의 자릿수는 숫자 맨 오른쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: The ones digit is at the far right of the number.

explain: '세 자리 수', '두 자리 숫자'처럼 '자리'로 세는 말이 더 흔해요. '자릿수'는 비밀번호나 계산에서 칸이 몇 개인지 말할 때 쓰고, '자릿수가 맞다', '자릿수가 모자라다'처럼 말해요. 소리는 [자리쑤]로 나요.

phrases.en: Please check that the number of digits in the card number is right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자 칸의 개수가 맞을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the number of digit places is correct.

phrases.example: 전화번호의 자릿수가 모자라서 전화가 안 걸려요.
phrases.en: The phone number has too few digits, so the call won't go through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자가 덜 들어갔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fewer digits were entered than needed.

phrases.en: One hundred is a three-digit number.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자릿수'보다 일상에서 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in everyday speech than '자릿수.'

explain_en: Koreans often count with 자리, as in '세 자리 수' (a three-digit number). 자릿수 is used for how many places a password or calculation has, as in '자릿수가 맞다' or '자릿수가 모자라다'. It is pronounced [자리쑤].

examples.en: In math class I learned that the square root of 9 is 3.
Please tell me how to find a square root.
I knew right away that the square root of 16 is 4.
The square root problem was hard, so I asked my teacher.

examples.ko: 숫자의 제곱근과 제곱은 서로 반대 개념이에요.
examples.en: The square root and the square of a number are opposite concepts.

examples.ko: 시험에 제곱근 계산이 나올 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think square root calculations will be on the test.

explain: '제곱'과 짝이 되는 말로, 제곱해서 그 수가 되는 수를 찾는 개념이에요. 'a의 제곱근'처럼 말하고, 기호 √는 수업에서 '루트'라고 읽기도 해요. 수학 수업이나 시험에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I found the square root with a calculator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 문제를 풀 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when solving math problems.

phrases.en: The square roots of 9 are 3 and -3.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수+의 제곱근'으로 어떤 수의 제곱근을 말해요. 양수의 제곱근은 보통 두 개예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pattern 'number + 의 제곱근' names the square roots of a number; a positive number usually has two.

phrases.en: I learned how to write the square root sign.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기호 √를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the symbol √.

explain_en: It is the partner of '제곱' (square): you look for the number that gives the original number when squared. You say it as 'the 제곱근 of a', and the symbol √ is also read aloud as '루트' in class. It comes up often in math lessons and exams.

examples.en: If you add up the scores for each item, you get the total score.
The total score for the exam is out of 100.
People with the higher total score get selected first.
Please calculate the total score of the two subjects.
Passing is decided by the total score.
I was five points short on the total score, so I failed.

explain: 여러 점수를 모두 더한 합계예요. 가능한 가장 높은 점수는 '만점'이라고 하니 총점과 헷갈리지 마세요. 점수를 사람 수나 과목 수로 나눈 값은 '평균'이에요.

phrases.en: The student with the highest total score gets a scholarship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수의 합계가 크다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the sum of scores is large.

phrases.en: I add up the scores for each subject to calculate the total.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 모두 더하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for adding up all the scores.

phrases.en: I got 180 out of a total of 200 points.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전체 점수와 받은 점수를 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the points you got out of the total.

explain_en: It's the sum of several scores. The highest possible score is '만점', so don't mix it up with 총점. The value divided by the number of people or subjects is '평균' (average).

examples.ko: 아이가 생기니까 학군을 보고 이사를 갔어요.
examples.en: After we had a child, we moved with the school district in mind.
This neighborhood is famous for its good schools.
House prices rose a lot because of the school district.

examples.ko: 학군이 같은 친구들끼리 한 학교에 모여요.
examples.en: Friends from the same district gather at one school.

examples.ko: 부모님은 좋은 학군에 사는 게 중요하다고 하세요.
examples.en: My parents say living in a good school district matters.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 학군이 달라서 그 학교에 못 가요.
examples.en: Our house is in a different district, so I can't go to that school.

explain: '학군이 좋다'는 부모가 이사할 집을 고를 때 많이 하는 말이에요. 좋은 학교가 모여 있는 곳은 '학군지'라고도 해요. 한국에서는 집값과 자주 같이 이야기해요.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a home in a good school district area so I can move there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 학교가 모인 지역을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an area where good schools are concentrated.

phrases.en: I want to live in a neighborhood with a good school district.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사할 곳을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about where to move.

phrases.en: I consider the school district when I choose a home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 조건 중에 학군을 꼼꼼히 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when carefully weighing the school district among other conditions.

explain_en: 학군이 좋다 is something parents say a lot when choosing where to move. An area with many good schools is also called 학군지. In Korea it is often discussed together with housing prices.
